How to Increase Car Fuel Average from 9 KM/L to 17 KM/L? | Biggest Reasons for High Fuel Consumption
Is your car consuming too much petrol? Are you getting only 9 KM/L fuel average instead of 15 to 17 KM/L? In this video, I will explain the biggest reasons for high fuel consumption and how you can improve your car's fuel average with proper inspection, diagnosis, and maintenance.
Many car owners complain that their vehicles consume too much petrol, even after regular servicing. But do you know that a small problem in the engine, fuel system, sensors, or ignition system can significantly reduce fuel efficiency?
In this detailed video, I explain the important things you should check when your car gives poor fuel average.
Topics Covered in This Video:

Biggest reasons for high fuel consumption.

How to improve car fuel average.

Why does a car consume too much petrol?

Faulty spark plugs and ignition coils.

Dirty or blocked air filter problems.

Fuel injector cleaning and testing.

Fuel pump pressure and fuel delivery problems.

Oxygen sensor problems and their effects on fuel consumption.

Faulty engine sensors and incorrect sensor readings.

Engine tuning and maintenance.

How to identify the reasons for poor fuel economy.

How to check your vehicle using a diagnostic scanner.

Important tips to improve petrol mileage.

Common mistakes that increase fuel consumption.

Why Is Your Car Giving Poor Fuel Average?
If your car is giving only 8, 9, or 10 KM/L, there may be several reasons behind this problem. A faulty oxygen sensor, dirty injectors, incorrect fuel pressure, damaged spark plugs, blocked air filters, or incorrect engine sensor readings can affect fuel efficiency.
Sometimes the problem is not related to one particular part. Multiple small problems can combine and cause excessive fuel consumption.
How to Improve Fuel Average?
Before replacing any expensive parts, always perform a proper inspection. Check the engine condition, air filter, spark plugs, fuel injectors, oxygen sensor readings, fuel pressure, and other important engine parameters.
A proper diagnosis can help you identify the actual problem and avoid unnecessary expenses.
Watch this complete video to understand how to diagnose high fuel consumption and improve your car's fuel efficiency.
If you are an automotive technician, mechanic, or car owner, this video will help you understand important reasons behind poor fuel economy.
Which Cars Can Benefit From These Tips?
These diagnostic tips are useful for many petrol vehicles, including:

Suzuki WagonR

Suzuki Alto

Suzuki Cultus

Toyota Corolla

Honda Civic

Honda City

Other petrol engine vehicles

Important: Actual fuel average depends on vehicle condition, engine size, driving habits, traffic conditions, road conditions, and maintenance. Increasing fuel average from 9 to 17 KM/L is not guaranteed for every vehicle. Always diagnose the actual problem before replacing parts.

Hello everyone today we will see the comon problem of high fuel ⛽ consumption on a car and how to solve it the problem.

Defective fuel injectors

If your fuel injectors are faulty and insufficient fuel is being injected into the engine, your car won’t run efficiently. A less efficient engine means increased fuel consumption.

Clogged air filters

Air filters and oxygen sensors ensure that the ratio of air and fuel going into the engine is correct for optimum performance. If they’re clogged or damaged, the ratio is affected, which can damage your engine and will increase the amount of fuel your car is using.
Faulty spark plugs

If the spark plugs in your car aren’t sparking correctly due to wear and tear or damage, it affects combustion. The result? Increased fuel consumption.

The wrong oil

If you aren’t using an oil that reduces friction or the oil recommended by the manufacturer of your vehicle, you could be paying the price with poor fuel economy.
